BiblicalUsage: The word is a fright, and also a granary, and it is used where God chooses what men fear and where He asks whether the seed is yet in the barn: Isaiah says God will choose their delusions and bring their fears upon them, and Haggai asks if the seed is yet in the barn, before the blessing comes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word holds the two sides of fear together: God brings on men the very things they feared, and He asks whether the seed is in the barn — because the harvest depends on what was sown, not on what was feared.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
